headings.title: SMTO-CTR-0012 — A check found the task plan adds a change you didn't ask for

html:
SMTO-CTR-0012 — A check found the task plan adds a change you didn't ask for

GUID: 43449ecc-1a99-4287-bf2c-a3f440c98882
Slug: task-contract-new-mutation
Domain: CTR · Subsystem: task-contract

What happened

  • A separate check of a Task Contract (the plan SMTO writes from a request) found it would delete, remove, restart, install or overwrite something your request never asked for. The check didn't run or change anything.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reread your request. If you didn't ask SMTO to delete, remove, restart, reboot, install or overwrite anything, treat this plan as wrong and don't use it. The plan includes a change your request never mentioned, and running it could alter things you wanted left alone.
  2. If you do want that change, say it plainly in the request, for example "restart the web service". If you wrote "don't" do something, keep that wording clear and separate. The check only accepts changes that your own words ask for, and treats anything you ruled out as forbidden.
  3. Send the request again as a new message so SMTO writes a new plan, and keep Task Contract Integrity Guard switched on. A new plan is checked from scratch, while turning the guard off would let risky plans through instead of fixing this one.

What success looks like

  • The check passes for the new Task Contract, or the new task shows Task contract generated and starts working.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with your request text, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't run a plan that deletes, restarts or installs things you didn't ask for.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Offline validate_contract found a mutating verb (delete, remove, restart, reboot, install, chmod, chown, truncate or overwrite) in the contract's action text that the accepted source does not authorize, or a verb the source prohibits stated as an affirmative action.

What this means

  • Offline action inspection finds a listed mutating verb absent from accepted authority, or a prohibited action appears as an affirmative action line. This condition is produced by an explicit offline contract diagnostic, not the current compiler acceptance gate. It reports only the named check and cannot authorize execution or prove complete semantic fidelity.

Why this can happen

  • Offline action inspection finds a listed mutating verb absent from accepted authority, or a prohibited action appears as an affirmative action line.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the action and any negation with original source intent before accepting a correction.

How to fix it

  • validate_contract in src/agent_runtime/native/task_contract_models.py raised new_mutation: a mutation verb in the objective, stage objectives or requirement descriptions is absent from the source, prior contract and ingress material, or the source negates it ('do not ...') while an action line states it. Regenerate or correct the contract so it contains only source-authorized actions, keep the Integrity Guard enabled, and remember this offline diagnostic (used by scripts/task_contract_benchmark.py) is not the compiler acceptance gate.
  • Correct the contract against the original intended operation without granting the added mutation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The contract's intended changes stay within the source's authorization.

What not to do

  • Do not disable the integrity guard as a default fix.

Technical notes

  • This condition is produced by an explicit offline contract diagnostic, not the current compiler acceptance gate. It reports only the named check and cannot authorize execution or prove complete semantic fidelity.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
